note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Start with Bob Harms' authentic connected fibrous-rooted grass and narrow flowering culms in gallery panel 1 (index 0); the source also shows a scale and spikelet inset. Find source-identified small field tufts in panels 9–10 (indices 8–9), and compare the same-species flowering positions in panel 4 (index 3). The annual lifecycle is supported by Flora of North America/Kew and cannot be proven solely by a photograph taken at one instant; Hays locality/voucher not confirmed.
tiles.short: Fine annual tuft; terminal AND upper-sheath heads
tiles.status: CONNECTED ROOTED WHOLE PLANT + FLOWERING CULM PHOTOGRAPHED — HAYS VOUCHER UNVERIFIED

tiles.heading: 02 · INNER LIGULE AND LEAVES
tiles.details: Actual original regional collar macro appears in Bob Harms panel 8 (index 7), and Wendy A's field sheath junction in panel 2 (index 1). New licensed Stefan.lefnaer gallery panel 15 (index 14) shows FIVE exterior blade/sheath junctions with a photographed 10-mm ruler; Harms upper sheaths at panel 3 (index 2) supply matched orientation. None yet exposes a calibrated 0.1–0.3-mm free INNER hair fringe. Do not label a sheath hair tuft or pale exterior ridge as a proved true ligule.
tiles.short: Very short hair fringe, not a tall membrane
tiles.status: MULTIPLE REAL COLLARS AT SCALE — TINY FREE INNER HAIR LIGULE STILL UNRESOLVED

tiles.heading: 03 · ONE MATURE SPIKELET
tiles.details: The mature one-floret spikelet and its pointed bracts are visible in Bob Harms panel 6 (index 5). NEW exact-source Wikimedia CC BY-SA 4.0 images appear in panels 13–14 (indices 12–13): Stefan.lefnaer shows a photographed spikelet at TWO sides with his own labels and 3-mm scale (sl125), and EIGHT different faces with a 5-mm scale (sl126). These are authentic *S. vaginiflorus* sensu Fischer et al. (2008) from AUSTRIA; they teach gross spikelet anatomy but do not provide a documented Texas/Hays voucher or proof of 400× fertile-lemma hairs.
tiles.short: Usually 3–5 mm; one floret and no true awn
tiles.status: MEASURED AUTHOR-LABELED SPIKELET PANELS NOW ARCHIVED — LOCAL VOUCHER + MICROHAIRS UNVERIFIED

tiles.heading: 04 · SEPARATE THE GLUMES AND LEMMA
tiles.details: The newly archived original photographs in panels 13–14 (indices 12–13) label and illustrate the lower glume (Glu'), upper glume (Glu\"), lemma (Lem), and palea (Pal) around a real mature spikelet, with 3-mm and 5-mm scales. This clears the BASIC photo teaching need for correctly named gross parts in a SOURCE-IDENTIFIED overseas population. Bob Harms panel 7 (index 6) remains useful for local-regional disarticulation, without exact per-bract arrows. Strict final Hays species separation still needs same-voucher lemma-hair/hook/silica microscopy against *S. neglectus* and *S. ozarkanus*; the photographed author labels do not establish that micromorphology.
tiles.short: Two basal glumes; pubescent fertile lemma
tiles.status: GROSS GLUME, LEMMA AND PALEA PHOTOGRAPHS WITH SCALE COVERED — 400× SPECIES DISCRIMINATOR OPEN

tiles.heading: 05 · UPPER-SHEATH FLOWERS
tiles.details: Harms SPVA-i in panel 4 (index 3) shows a real terminal spikelet-bearing panicle and SEPARATE shorter upper-sheath / axillary flowering clusters on the same photographed culm. The sheath exterior is visible in panel 3 (index 2). However, a mature floret still hidden *inside* an unopened sheath and a true self-pollination event are NOT documented in these pixels. A botanist-confirmed dissection before-and-after opening a sheath of one authenticated plant remains the required high-value photograph.
tiles.short: Do not infer cleistogamy from a hidden head
tiles.status: TWO ACTUAL FLOWERING POSITIONS COVERED — CONCEALED CLEISTOGAMOUS FLORET UNPROVEN

tiles.heading: 06 · SMALL DROPSEED LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Existing gallery panel 11 (index 10) is *S. clandestinus* and panel 12 (index 11) is *S. compositus*, both different species and generally perennial. New measured spikelet photos 13–14 (indices 12–13) show Austrian source-defined *S. vaginiflorus* anatomy, NOT same-maturity Texas *S. neglectus* or *S. ozarkanus*. S. neglectus may share annual tuft and hidden upper-sheath flowers but has smaller spikelets, often ~1.5–3 mm, and largely hairless lemma/palea in classical treatments. The ozarkanus taxon/rank has active scientific conflicts: preserve canonical taxonomy holds and demand vouchered lemma pubescence/veins before split.
tiles.short: Pubescent lemma matters more than head outline
tiles.status: ACTUAL COMPOSITUS/CLANDESTINUS COMPARISON PHOTOS — NEGLECTUS/OZARKANUS SAME-SCALE MICRO MATCH MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: POVERTY DROPSEED (*Sporobolus vaginiflorus*): SEE attached fibrous ROOTS and flowering stems on Bob Harms SPVA-b1 (gallery panel 1); then actual terminal and upper-sheath flower cluster positions on SPVA-i (panel 4). True grass hair ligule is an extremely short inner fringe, not a long membrane. NEW 2026 credited Commons anatomical plates in panels 13–14 show labelled LOWER/UPPER GLUMES, LEMMA and PALEA of a 3–5mm single-floret spikelet with 3mm/5mm photographed scale. Those photographer-identified European images are diagnostic teaching references, NOT proof of a Hays specimen or resolution of the S. ozarkanus/neglectus rank complex. Keep fully enclosed cleistogamy and 400× lemma hooks/hairs as separate required verification.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: ACTUAL ROOTS: Bob Harms SPVA-b1 in panel 1 (index 0) physically connects fine fibrous roots, leafy basal crown and several flowering culms. Its author's taxon ID is recorded, but site-specific Hays voucher and the full annual lifecycle are not established by one photograph.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Actual original regional collar macro appears in Bob Harms panel 8 (index 7), and Wendy A's field sheath junction in panel 2 (index 1). New licensed Stefan.lefnaer gallery panel 15 (index 14) shows FIVE exterior blade/sheath junctions with a photographed 10-mm ruler; Harms upper sheaths at panel 3 (index 2) supply matched orientation. None yet exposes a calibrated 0.1–0.3-mm free INNER hair fringe. Do not label a sheath hair tuft or pale exterior ridge as a proved true ligule.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: The mature one-floret spikelet and its pointed bracts are visible in Bob Harms panel 6 (index 5). NEW exact-source Wikimedia CC BY-SA 4.0 images appear in panels 13–14 (indices 12–13): Stefan.lefnaer shows a photographed spikelet at TWO sides with his own labels and 3-mm scale (sl125), and EIGHT different faces with a 5-mm scale (sl126). These are authentic *S. vaginiflorus* sensu Fischer et al. (2008) from AUSTRIA; they teach gross spikelet anatomy but do not provide a documented Texas/Hays voucher or proof of 400× fertile-lemma hairs.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

intro: POVERTY DROPSEED (*Sporobolus vaginiflorus*): SEE attached fibrous ROOTS and flowering stems on Bob Harms SPVA-b1 (gallery panel 1); then actual terminal and upper-sheath flower cluster positions on SPVA-i (panel 4). memory_rule: POVERTY DROPSEED: tiny short-lived fine-leaved grass with ROOTED FIBROUS base, narrow terminal panicle plus additional upper leaf-SHEATH inflorescences. Spikelet contains ONE floret, ligule SHORT double HAIR fringe (ca. 0.1–0.3mm). S. neglectus/ozarkanus complex needs true mature lemma microtexture, not one habit picture.
safety_note: 13 physically archived EXACT SPECIES JPEGs (8 Harms, 2 earlier local, 3 new Stefan), plus 2 other species look-alike panels, 15 total gallery. One historical illustration remains remote outside gallery. Critical scientific holds: tiny 0.1–0.3mm inner true ligule, proof of enclosed upper-sheath floret, true 400× hairs/hooks vs S. neglectus/ozarkanus, local vouchered specimen, live Pages validation.
field_rule: Use visible macro morphology first and defer difficult perennial-species separations to mature material, reliable grain tests and microscope when necessary.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
